item.description:
**Download:** [Leise-2.2.2.zip](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise/releases/download/v2.2.2/Leise-2.2.2.zip) — quit Leise, then replace the old `Leise.app` in your Applications folder. (First launch after replacing: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway", same as before — [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).)
## What changed in 2.2.2
- **Numbers dictate as digits — in German too.** Chinese numerals next to a Latin letter convert (`V 四` → `V4`), telecom readings convert (`幺三幺` → `131`), multi-digit decimals with units convert (`四点九三GB` → `4.93GB`), and mixed forms like `二点.二点一` → `2.2.1` or `二点儿零` → `2.0` finally land as written. German spoken numbers join the same rule: *vier Punkt drei neunzig KB* → `4.93 KB`, *zwei Minuten* → `2 minutes`, with both *Komma* and *Punkt* recognised. - **A microphone that disappears mid-dictation no longer ends it.** If the current input vanishes while you speak, Leise switches to another connected device and keeps everything captured so far — the notice names the device it switched to. (If none is available, the recording is delivered as before.) - **Re-transcribe a bad result from its recording.** History rows gain a Re-transcribe action: the row's own audio is run through today's engine and polish chain, and the result is appended as a new row — the original is never overwritten. - **Replacement rules can be taught by hand again.** The Rules tab's plus opens an add-rule card running the same acceptance gates as the learner, and the tab now says what its two layers are: dictionary words bias the recogniser, rewrite rules force the substitution. - **Settings → General → Backup.** Export everything you have tuned — dictionary, prompts, hotkeys, polish exclusions, preferences — as a single file, and import it again after a reinstall. Importing previews what will change, snapshots your current settings first, and a failed import leaves everything untouched. - **The polish model keeps your language.** The polish instructions now state explicitly that output stays in the language spoken — never translated in either direction — and name three cleanups that used to slip through: stuttered repetitions, uncued restatements, and punctuation the recogniser planted inside a word. - **The learned-term banner is back, where you are looking.** It appears next to the field you just corrected instead of at the bottom of the screen, and Settings → General gains a "Show learning notifications" toggle — on by default; off means learning continues silently in the background. - **History stays live and copies cleanly.** The History page follows the store while it is open (no restart to see new dictations), each row grows a hover Copy button, and a duplicate-insert repair that used to fail open now fails closed. - **Engine memory under control.** Both models no longer stay resident all working day: under memory pressure the recognition model yields and reloads on demand (the 9/12 memory squeeze). The engine log gained timestamps and a memory curve, and a vanished update client logs one quiet line instead of a traceback page. - **Fixed for macOS 14/15.** The published app shipped macOS-26-only model wheels and needed a Homebrew ffmpeg — on older Macs every dictation failed. Both are fixed; Leise 2.2.2 works on the macOS 14.4+ the README promises. (Found by a tester — thank you.)
## The essentials (unchanged)
**Apple Silicon only** (M1 or newer) · **macOS 14.4+** · about **7 GB free disk** (523 MB app + 5.9 GB speech models downloaded on first run).
A 100 % local dictation app for macOS. Your audio and your transcripts never leave your Mac; it works with the network off.
**macOS will refuse to open it once.** Leise is signed but not notarised. ⛔ **In both dialogs the blue default button is "Move to Trash"** — pressing Return deletes the app you just downloaded. Click **Done**, then go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, find the line about Leise, and click **Open Anyway**. Full walkthrough in English, Deutsch and 简体中文: [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).
**What it sends over the network.** Nothing about you. The speech models on first run, and — only if you enable update checks, which ships off — a version-number request to the update feed. Both under your control.
If you are coming from 2.2.0: 2.2.1 was never published, so 2.2.2 contains everything above plus the intermediate fixes — a reconnection guard for the update question, the single install slot with a running-instance guard, and the cleaned-up factory check.
Anything wrong: **Settings → General → Diagnostics → Export Diagnostics** writes a file to your Downloads folder. Send it over.
